gaps.sentence: The scheme aims ___ younger visitors to the museum.
gaps.explanation: aim + to-infinitive: aims to attract (aim at + -ing is also possible in BrE).

gaps.sentence: I want you ___ the truth, whatever it is.
gaps.explanation: want + object + to-infinitive: want you to tell.
seem/appear take the to-infinitive: seems to know.

gaps.sentence: I can't wait ___ you the photos.
gaps.explanation: can't wait + to-infinitive: can't wait to show.

gaps.sentence: We stopped at a village ___ some lunch.
gaps.explanation: stop to do = pause in order to do something: stopped to have lunch.

gaps.sentence: The witness claims ___ the getaway car parked outside for an hour.
gaps.explanation: 'Claims to have seen' — the perfect infinitive marks an earlier action.

gaps.sentence: We're thinking of ___ to the coast for the weekend.
